transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-12
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Kim (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Rachel Torres (Crestline Head of Platform), Imran Patel (Crestline SRE), Lena Ortiz (Cloud Security), Daniel Cho (Procurement)

Summary (auto): Quick renewal + expansion sync. Discussed Dedicated capacity options, region expansion, latency expectations, security docs, and procurement timeline. Agreed on action items to share pricing, benchmarks, and security supplements.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Kim: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um we know you've got renewal coming up next month so wanted to go through expansion asks and make sure we align on capacity and regions. Rachel, is this still a 30k monthly token baseline that we're planning off?
[00:12] Rachel Torres: Yeah morning Sofia. Yep, baseline still about 30k tokens a month but we're seeing spikes on payroll and statements so peak QPS could be higher, like 6 to 8 rps during 9–11am ET.
[00:23] Imran Patel: And just to add, the latency at p95 matters more than avg for us, we've had a couple of incidents where a backend headroom caused timeouts.
[00:31] Marcus Lee: Got it, p95 latency SLOs — noted. When we scoped the Dedicated plan last year we sized GPUs for your steady throughput not the burst profile. For bursts we recommend either burst capacity or autoscale config; both are options.
[00:44] Rachel Torres: On the burst capacity, how do we think about cost? We want predictable unit economics, and don't want a surprise bill.
[00:52] Sofia Kim: Totally. We can provide two options — reserved baseline plus a capped burst pool (monthly cap), or a higher reserved commit with lower per-token overage. We'll send a 12 vs 24 month ROI which shows break-even points.
[01:05] Daniel Cho: Procurement will want that in writing; also need the contract extension language. Can you include termination windows and credits for downtimes?
[01:12] Sofia Kim: Yes we'll include SLA language and a sample amendment. Marcus will also point to our historical uptime numbers.
[01:19] Lena Ortiz: Quick security note — we're moving more workloads into EU and looking at APAC pilot late Q3. We need to confirm data residency and KMS/HSM integration. Do you have a private deployment option for on-prem or VPC?
[01:33] Marcus Lee: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed VPC and on-prem bundle. We integrate with KMS providers — we've got docs for AWS KMS, GCP KMS and HSM patterns. One caveat, when you use HSM for key wrapping there is an additional setup window and rotation overhead.
[01:48] Rachel Torres: Do you have a SOC2 supplement and details on audit logs? Our compliance team will ask.
[01:54] Sofia Kim: We'll attach SOC2 type II report and a supplement that outlines audit log retention, who can access, and RBAC examples. Lena, Marcus can also share sample log schemas.
[02:05] Imran Patel: For the APAC region — what's the model catalogue there? We need to ensure models are consistent across regions to avoid output variance.
[02:13] Marcus Lee: Good question. We generally replicate the same model variants, but sometimes we use quantized variants for cost/latency tradeoffs. That can introduce small output diffs; we can pin model versions and use rollouts to test. Also note, quantization profiles are tuned per hardware, so minor differences may occur.
[02:30] Rachel Torres: Hmm, output variance is a risk for us. Is there a way to force identical outputs?
[02:34] Marcus Lee: Short answer: exact bitwise identical outputs is hard across hardware and quantization. But for user-facing consistency we do stable seeds, model pinning, and controlled rollouts with evals. We'll run a canary across EU and APAC and report regressions on your eval set.
[02:48] Sofia Kim: We'll include a suggested rollout plan in the doc with canary percentages and monitoring hooks.
[02:54] Daniel Cho: On pricing — if we expand to EU and APAC, can we get region bundling discounts or a multi-region commitment?
[03:01] Sofia Kim: Yes, multi-region commits can be structured. We typically do a regional uplift or a single global commit with discounted tiers for additional regions. We'll model a few scenarios in the ROI sheet.
[03:11] Rachel Torres: For the benchmarks, Marcus, can you re-run the 8k token profile with our typical prompt set and share observed p50/p95 and GPU utilization? Last time the transcript had some weird mislabeling — the KV cache was misread in the notes — so just want raw logs.
[03:25] Marcus Lee: Absolutely. I'll re-run the 8k seq profile against the dedicated hardware profile and share the perf dashboard link. I'll include p50/p95/99, throughput, batch sizes, and KV cache hit rates — excuse my voice, the transcriber sometimes writes K-V catche which is hilarious.
[03:39] Imran Patel: Please also include cold start numbers and how long the KV warmup is after a burst. We've seen slowdowns after idle periods.
[03:46] Marcus Lee: Will do — we'll include warmup curves and recommended cache TTLs.
[03:50] Rachel Torres: On the security integration timeline, how long does Redwood Private setup take if we want VPC and KMS?
[03:56] Marcus Lee: Typical is 4–6 weeks for VPC peering, KMS integration and initial deployment. If you want an on-prem appliance there's additional provisioning time. We can compress timelines with a parallel network setup if your infra team is ready.
[04:10] Lena Ortiz: We also need answers about key custody: does Redwood ever see plaintext?
[04:14] Sofia Kim: No, with customer-managed KMS we do not have access to plaintext keys. We can provide cryptographic proof-of-setup walkthroughs and an HSM attestation summary for audit.
[04:24] Daniel Cho: Ok procurement will want those in the package.
[04:27] Sofia Kim: Sounds good. Any blockers on pricing or timeline from your side right now?
[04:31] Rachel Torres: Not blockers, just need the numbers so we can model the budget for Q4. Also want a proposal for 12 vs 24 month term pricing and a note on credits for SLA misses.
[04:40] Sofia Kim: We'll include both terms in the proposal and a sample SLA credit table.
[04:44] Marcus Lee: One more technical note — if you plan heavy bursty traffic, an autoscale policy that pre-warms additional instances at 70% CPU can help avoid p95 spikes, but it does increase cost. We'll model that in the cost table.
[04:58] Imran Patel: For evaluation, can Redwood run a short PoC in EU using our eval set so we can validate quality before we commit?
[05:05] Sofia Kim: Yes, we can do a short PoC. We usually do a 2-week pilot with production traffic mirror for a limited set of routes, and help run A/B between current hosted model and dedicated instance. Marcus will scope the PoC steps.
[05:16] Marcus Lee: I'll prepare a PoC plan: target routes, sample size, metrics (latency, cost per token, regression delta on eval prompts), and required access.
[05:25] Rachel Torres: Great. Would like the PoC to include a simulated APAC latence — i.e., validate region routing.
[05:30] Marcus Lee: Noted. We'll spin up canary nodes in EU and APAC test regions.
[05:34] Sofia Kim: Ok quick recap: we will send updated pricing with 12/24 month comparisons, Marcus shares benchmarks and PoC plan, Lena gets SOC2 supplement and KMS/HSM notes, Rachel confirms regions by 7/20, and Daniel checks procurement timeline.
[05:48] Daniel Cho: That's right. Also we'll appreciate a one-pager for legal on contract amendment language.
[05:55] Sofia Kim: We'll include a sample amendment and SLA language.
[06:00] Rachel Torres: Thanks all, this was useful. Any final Qs?
[06:03] Imran Patel: No, just please make sure warmup numbers are explicit.
[06:06] Marcus Lee: Will do.
[06:08] Sofia Kim: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and action items.
[06:11] (call ends)

Notes: Transcription has occasional mis-heard terms and inconsistent punctuation; the speakers sometimes overlap. References to artifacts: "Dedicated pricing spreadsheet" (to be sent), "benchmark logs" (link), "SOC2 supplement" (PDF).
